newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slip with U.S. mkt in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slip with U.S. mkt in quiet trade.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished slightly lower Tuesday, following a decline in U.S. Treasuries amid slow trade.
"There was very little trade," said a trader at a local bank. "There was little movement."
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 fell 1/8 to 92-7/8 whilethe dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 slipped $0.02 to 122.95.
Players did not expect the market to pick up much steam in coming days but rather continue to tag the performance of U.S. Treasuries ahead of important data releases next week.

Another trader pointed out the market "is at very high levels," currently, something which could lead to selling pressures later this week if the U.S. 30-year bond yield rises further above 7.0 percent.
The U.S. 30-year yield rose three basis points to 7.02 percent Tuesday.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 5.88 percent from 5.73 percent.
